newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai Motor resumes exports to Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai Motor resumes exports to Taiwan.

text.p: South Korea's largest car maker, Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, said on Monday it has resumed car exports to Taiwan for the first time since 1992 when Seoul and Taipei severed diplomatic ties.
Hyundai Motor said it shipped 270 automobiles on Monday.
Taiwan banned car imports from South Korea after Seoul cut diplomatic ties with Taipei to normalise relations with China in October 1992.

Hyundai said it had prepared for the resumption of business in Taiwan since Tapei lifted the ban late in 1996. Kia Motors Corp, South Korea's second largest carmaker, exported 700 cars to Taiwan last year, a trade ministry official said.
Hyundai said it was currently operating a total of 18 showrooms and 30 service centres in Taiwan.
Hyundai Motor, a unit of the Hyundai Group, plans to export a total of 2,848 cars to Taiwan this year through its local agent, Jack Wang Motor Co, it said.
